description:
Reducing over a Map hands the reducer an element typed `{any, any}` instead of
the map's known key/value types. The operand reaches `Kernel.+/2` as `any` and
the reducer's return widens from `int` to `int | float`. Reducing over a
structurally identical LIST OF TUPLES keeps full precision, which isolates the
defect to the Map Enumerable element boundary.

## Repro

    fn main() do
      dbg(Enum.reduce(%{:a => 1}, 0, fn ({_k, v}, acc) -> v + acc end))
    end

prints `1` and dumps (`--dump activations`):

    #lambda:0:46-78/2[{any, any}, int]
      return: int | float
      callsites:  @67-74 => Kernel.+/2(any, int) => int | float
    main/0[]
      callsites:  @19-79 => Enum.reduce/3(%{:a: int}, int, ...) => int

CONTROL -- replace `%{:a => 1}` with `[{:a, 1}]`, everything else identical:

    #lambda:0:45-77/2[{:a, int}, int]
      return: int
      callsites:  @66-73 => Kernel.+/2(int, int) => int

The receiver's own type is precise in BOTH cases (`%{:a: int}`), so the loss is
in how the Map Enumerable impl types the element it yields, not in how the map
is inferred.

ELIXIR: `Enum.reduce(%{:a => 1, :b => 2}, 0, fn {_k, v}, acc -> v + acc end)`
returns 3; fz returns 3 too. The runtime answer is CORRECT. This is purely lost
precision -- it costs specialization and monomorphic extern selection, not
correctness.

## What the old ticket got wrong

It was filed against the whole operator cluster (`+/2 */2 -/2 %/2 fz_op_add/
mul/sub/rem_*, fz_binary_concat`) with "~600 hits, DOMINANT".

- The operator cluster is now CLEAN everywhere observable. Range, List,
  list-of-tuples, int, float and binary accumulators all show
  `Kernel.+/2(int, int) => int`, and the backend selects the monomorphic
  externs `fz_op_add_ii` / `fz_op_mul_ii`, which it could not do from `any`.
- Both roots it named as blockers have CLOSED: fz-f98.10 (protocol-domain
  erasure) and fz-f98.12 (pid at send). Its own prediction -- "likely largely
  resolved by fixing the roots" -- is now measurably about 90% correct.
- The ~600 figure came from fz-f98.9's graduation warning, which was never
  implemented (`grep -rn GRADUATED src/` is empty), so it cannot be
  re-measured. Do not plan against it.

DO NOT treat the operator sites as the subject. The Map element boundary is.

## Coverage limit of this measurement

`--dump activations` filters to root-owned code (`root_owned_activations`,
dump.rs:237-249), so a graduated `any` on a prelude-internal parameter -- say
`reduce_cont/5` -- would be invisible. Everything observable is concrete; the
prelude interior is unmeasured.

## Checks

- The repro dumps `#lambda[{:a, int}, int]` and `Kernel.+/2(int, int) => int`,
  matching the list control.
- `fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz` currently shows
  `Enum.take/2([int], int) => [int] | [any] | []` when List and Range sources
  mix; that `[any]` arm is the sibling return-position instance of the same
  element erasure and should disappear too.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.

Not in scope: do not fix at the operator, and do not special-case Map -- the fix
belongs where the Map Enumerable impl types its yielded element.
title: Map's Enumerable element type erases to a tuple of any, graduating reducer operands before Kernel arithmetic
